scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The IT and CS departments have been CUT OFF from
each other!! From it_hod, the department head's machine, none of the CS
computers on 192.168.2.x answer any more -- our own department is fine, it's
just CS that's gone. Something around the router that joins the two
departments must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and
rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation found no fault at any layer. The topology has router0 directly bridging the IT subnet (192.168.1.0/24 on eth0) and the CS subnet (192.168.2.0/24 on eth1). The kernel routing table on router0 carries both as directly-connected routes, IP forwarding is enabled (ip_forward=1), and FRR's zebra is running with an otherwise empty configuration — consistent with a static/kernel-only routing design that needs no OSPF.

A live ICMP probe from it_hod (192.168.1.2) to cs_hod (192.168.2.2) completed with 0% packet loss and TTL=63, confirming exactly one routing hop through router0 in each direction. No nftables/iptables rules exist on any of the 30 scanned devices (infra_sweep, 0 ACL fingerprints), ruling out selective protocol filtering. Traffic shaping is absent (tc_snapshot: all 43 interfaces use the default fq_codel qdisc). No stress or flap process was detected by pressure_sweep. No carrier-loss or interface-down events appear in router0's dmesg, and the syslog is empty. The dhcp_link_history sweep found no historical anomalies on any device.

Root cause: The claimed IT↔CS connectivity failure is unconfirmed — no fault mechanism exists in the running lab and no historical trace (log entry, carrier counter, or flap process) corroborates a past transient. The IT and CS departments can communicate normally through router0 right now.

Fix: No corrective action is required. If the user observed an issue, it may have been a transient ARP miss at lab startup that self-resolved; advise them to retry their workflow and report back if the problem recurs with specific error messages.
